When the church at Antioch 'sent on their way' Paul and Barnabas (Acts 15:3), or when Ephesian elders accompanied Paul to the ship (Acts 20:38), the word carries overtones of communal care and prayerful farewell. Paul himself hopes to be 'sent on' by the Roman church toward Spain (Rom 15:24). German 'geleiten' (escort, conduct) and Spanish 'acompañar' (accompany) both capture the personal, relational dimension that distinguishes this word from mere dispatching."
